text:
The second overall pick in 2025 is still 19, and San Jose has started trusting Michael Misa with more. He played about 16 minutes a night over his last ten games, nearly three more than before, topping 20 against Minnesota. Ten points in 21 games, three on the power play, is a reasonable line for a teenager on a team that loses a lot.

His own game looks like a scorer's. He's getting 0.85 expected goals per 60 (the quality of his own chances) and shooting 14.8%, close to normal, so the goals aren't a fluke. He has the legs for it, too: 94th percentile on NHL EDGE for 20-plus mph bursts. His snap shot opening the scoring in Dallas on Nov. 7 was the kind of play the Sharks drafted him for.

The rough part is everything else at five-on-five. San Jose takes only 38% of the expected goals with him on the ice, more than seven points worse than without him. That's normal for a 19-year-old, and the main thing to watch as the minutes grow. San Jose Hockey Now is already asking how he earns more shootout trust, which tells you how quickly expectations have arrived.
